how_to_read: A shift of one number between the two result sets is 'expected' when a rule below covers its board, model, cell and metric and its direction and size are inside the bounds; 'to be explained' when the item is a plausible cause and no study gives the size; 'unexplained' when no rule covers it. A must_not_move entry wins over every rule. Sizes: abs_k in K, rel_rise as a fraction of the baseline rise of the hottest point, rel as a fraction of the baseline value (counts). Status: 'quantified' = the bound is a number printed by a study; 'derived' = the bound is worked out from a printed number or is an engineering margin; 'to be explained' = no size known. Everything not measured here is left as 'to be explained' on purpose.

must_not_move.reason: two layers of full copper, no vias and no outline: no item of 2.4.5 reaches them (the laminate rule is the earlier model bit for bit where copper is in every cell; a block keeps the earlier treatment)
Lumped and Analytic never change on a board without vias (the laminate rule does not reach them, an outline runs on the equivalent rectangle bit for bit, the via constriction needs a via)
the 3D solid changes only with an outline (I1, I2) or a via (I4); the laminate rule leaves it alone (it reports the centre of its top slab)
the unknown count of the 3D solid does not change in 2.4.5
the FDM already sampled the cover 8 x 8 and keeps the plain intersection for a part: its hottest point and field on a full-copper outline board do not move (only the read-outs of the means do)
copper in every cell: no laminate nodes are added and the point via adds no unknown
Lumped and Analytic never change on a board without vias
